name: Distributed Systems
description: How machines cooperate over unreliable networks: time and ordering, replication, consensus and distributed data.

nodes.name: Why distributed
nodes.desc: Scale, fault tolerance and latency, and the fallacies of distributed computing.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain why systems are distributed for scale, fault tolerance and latency, and recognise the fallacies of distributed computing.

nodes.name: Failure models
nodes.desc: Crash, omission and Byzantine failures, partial failure and partitions.
nodes.summary: You will be able to distinguish crash, omission and Byzantine failures and reason about partial failures and network partitions.

nodes.name: RPC & messaging
nodes.desc: Remote procedure calls, at-most-once vs at-least-once delivery and idempotency.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain remote procedure calls and messaging semantics and design idempotent operations for safe retries.

nodes.name: Physical clocks
nodes.desc: Clock drift, NTP and why wall-clock time cannot order events.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain clock drift and NTP synchronisation and why wall-clock time cannot reliably order events.

nodes.name: Logical clocks
nodes.desc: Happens-before, Lamport clocks and vector clocks.
nodes.summary: You will be able to order events with the happens-before relation using Lamport clocks and vector clocks.

nodes.name: Broadcast & ordering
nodes.desc: Reliable, FIFO, causal and total-order broadcast.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compare reliable, FIFO, causal and total-order broadcast and the guarantees each provides.

nodes.name: Replication
nodes.desc: Leader-follower, multi-leader and leaderless replication.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compare leader-follower, multi-leader and leaderless replication and their handling of lag and conflicts.

nodes.name: Consistency models
nodes.desc: Linearizability, sequential, causal and eventual consistency.
nodes.summary: You will be able to distinguish linearizability, sequential, causal and eventual consistency and the trade-offs captured by CAP.

nodes.name: Quorums
nodes.desc: Read and write quorums, sloppy quorums and anti-entropy.
nodes.summary: You will be able to choose read and write quorum sizes and explain sloppy quorums, hinted handoff and anti-entropy repair.

nodes.name: CRDTs
nodes.desc: Conflict-free replicated data types for coordination-free replication.
nodes.summary: You will be able to design conflict-free replicated data types that converge without coordination.

nodes.name: Consensus
nodes.desc: The consensus problem, FLP impossibility and why it underlies coordination.
nodes.summary: You will be able to state the consensus problem, explain the FLP impossibility result and why consensus underlies coordination.

nodes.name: Leader election
nodes.desc: Elections, terms, leases and avoiding split brain.
nodes.summary: You will be able to elect leaders safely using terms and leases while avoiding split brain.

nodes.name: Raft
nodes.desc: Raft's leader election, log replication and safety.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain Raft's leader election, log replication and safety rules.

nodes.name: Paxos
nodes.desc: Single-decree and Multi-Paxos.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how single-decree Paxos reaches agreement and how Multi-Paxos extends it to a log.

nodes.name: Byzantine faults
nodes.desc: Byzantine fault tolerance, PBFT and the 3f+1 bound.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain Byzantine fault tolerance, the 3f+1 bound and how PBFT reaches agreement.

nodes.name: Partitioning
nodes.desc: Range and hash partitioning, consistent hashing and rebalancing.
nodes.summary: You will be able to partition data by range or hash, apply consistent hashing and rebalance partitions across nodes.

nodes.name: 2PC & sagas
nodes.desc: Atomic commit with two-phase commit and long-running sagas.
nodes.summary: You will be able to implement atomic commit with two-phase commit and coordinate long-running workflows with sagas.

nodes.name: Distributed storage
nodes.desc: How systems like Dynamo, Bigtable and Spanner combine these ideas.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how Dynamo, Bigtable and Spanner combine partitioning, replication and consensus into real storage systems.

nodes.name: MapReduce & dataflow
nodes.desc: MapReduce, Spark-style dataflow and fault-tolerant batch processing.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain MapReduce and Spark-style dataflow and how they tolerate failures in batch processing.

nodes.name: Raft KV store project
nodes.desc: Implement Raft and build a replicated, fault-tolerant key-value store on it.
nodes.summary: You will implement Raft and build a replicated, fault-tolerant key-value store on top of it.
